fatal_errors: The proposed intervention is prolonged aging at 550–650 °C rather than consolidation by spark plasma sintering at 800–1000 °C.
It omits the key densification and oxide-barrier pathway involving uniformly distributed AlV2O4, FeAl2O4, and FeTiO3 phases.
The proposed Mg-rich intermetallic coarsening threshold and service boundaries are asserted without supporting evidence from reported Mg-containing alloys.
It does not test the target corrosion and oxidation regimes of 3.5 wt% NaCl and 900 °C air or the expected electrochemical and biphasic parabolic-oxidation signatures.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad unresolved issue of diffusional evolution from a metastable solid solution and supplies a reasonably discriminating time-series experiment with an explicit falsification rule. However, it reconstructs neither the material processing pathway nor the central mechanism. The target concerns SPS-driven densification at up to 1000 °C, formation of distributed oxide barrier phases, improved passivation against chloride penetration, and biphasic parabolic oxidation. The generated account instead posits an unsupported fine-to-coarse Mg-rich intermetallic transition during lower-temperature service aging. Its baseline is experimentally usable but differs from the relevant comparison among lower- and higher-temperature SPS specimens. The proposed 550–650 °C and >100 h boundary is speculative, and no reported-alloy evidence is cited. Thus it is a testable idea, but insufficiently supported and poorly matched to the target.
